headline: US Federal Reserve Raises Rates for First Time Since 2023
seoTitle: US Fed Raises Rates 25 Basis Points to 3.75%-4% | FMB News
seoDescription: The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest-rate target by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on September 16, its first increase since 2023, as officials said inflation remains elevated.
deck: The FOMC unanimously raised the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75%-4%. Reuters reports it is the first US rate increase in more than three years, with policymakers signaling that further tightening may follow.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The US Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest-rate target by 25 basis points on Wednesday, September 16, taking the federal funds target range to 3.75% to 4%.
The Federal Open Market Committee approved the move by a unanimous 12-0 vote. Reuters reported that it was the Fed's first rate increase in more than three years.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Federal Reserve's official statement says economic activity is expanding at a solid pace, domestic spending has been resilient, job gains have kept pace with the workforce and unemployment has changed little.

The central bank said inflation remains elevated and described the rate increase as supporting a timelier return to its 2% inflation goal. The accompanying implementation note makes the new operating rates effective September 17 in the United States.

sections.heading: What remains uncertain
paragraphs: The September projections indicate that policymakers collectively expect additional tightening, but projections are not promises and the future policy path can change with inflation, employment, financial conditions and geopolitical developments.
FMB News is therefore not treating any future rate increase as predetermined.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: US monetary policy affects borrowing costs, the dollar, global bond yields and capital flows. For economies including the Philippines, a higher US policy rate can influence exchange-rate and financing conditions, although the size and direction of those effects also depend on domestic policy and market conditions.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch incoming US inflation and labor-market data, statements from Federal Reserve officials, movements in the dollar and Treasury yields, and how other central banks respond to the changed global rate environment.

verificationNotes: The Federal Reserve's official September 16 FOMC statement confirms a unanimous 25-basis-point increase to a 3.75%-4% target range.
The Federal Reserve implementation note confirms the operational rates effective September 17.
Reuters independently reports that the move is the first Federal Reserve rate increase in more than three years and reports the signal of possible further tightening.
Future policy moves are described as uncertain rather than predetermined.

The hero is a Federal Reserve Board photograph hosted on Wikimedia Commons and explicitly identified as public domain in the United States because it is a work of the Board of Governors. The caption labels it as a file photograph rather than an image of the September meeting.
